subject: Climate & Environment
title: Glaciers as Water Towers
description: Learn Glaciers as Water Towers in one minute.

hook.text: Glaciers feed rivers that supply drinking water to 1.9 billion people worldwide.

buildup.text: In dry seasons, glacier melt keeps rivers flowing when rain stops.

discovery.text: The Himalayas alone supply water to 10 major river systems across Asia.

twist.text: Glaciers worldwide have lost over 9 trillion tons of ice since the 1960s.

climax.text: As glaciers shrink, rivers will surge with meltwater first — then dry up for good.

punchline.text: Glaciers are savings accounts. We are spending the last of them.

quiz.question: How many people depend on glacier-fed rivers for water?

details.summary: Mountain glaciers act as natural water towers, storing winter snowfall as ice and releasing meltwater throughout summer to feed rivers that billions of people depend on. As glaciers shrink under warming, seasonal water supply for agriculture, hydropower, and cities is at growing risk.
details.whyItMatters: Over a billion people in Asia alone rely on glacial meltwater. Losing these ice reserves threatens agriculture, energy production, and drinking water across entire continents.
takeaways: Glaciers store winter snow and release meltwater in summer
Over a billion people depend on glacial rivers for water
Glacial retreat reduces dry-season water supply

faq.question: Which rivers depend most on glacial melt?
faq.answer: The Indus, Ganges, Brahmaputra, Yangtze, and Mekong all originate in heavily glaciated mountain ranges. The Indus receives up to 40 percent of its flow from glacial melt. In dry years, this dependence increases further, making glacial loss particularly dangerous.

faq.question: What happens when glaciers disappear completely?
faq.answer: Initially, melt increases as glaciers shrink faster, creating temporary abundance. After passing peak water, rivers receive progressively less meltwater, reducing dry-season flows. Some Andean and Central Asian communities are already experiencing this decline.
